coordinates.quote: located about 3.6 km offshore at 51∘ 46'N and 104∘ 24'E coordinates

depth.quote: The lakebed reaches its plateau at a nearly constant depth of 1366 m
depth.note: The official INR RAS facility page states a broader '1100-1300 m' range for the historical Baikal neutrino experiment site; the 2023 status paper's 1366 m lakebed figure is used as the more specific, more recent value for the current Baikal-GVD clusters.

summary.plain: A spot near the shore of the southern end of Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, where strings of light sensors are anchored more than a kilometre deep in the world's deepest lake.
summary.technical: Southern basin of Lake Baikal, ~3.6 km offshore at 51°46'N 104°24'E, lakebed depth ~1366 m; site of the expanding Baikal-GVD neutrino telescope's clusters.
